title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-olivia-kim
content:
Notes to self / breadcrumbs for the model loading failure seen on dedicated staging (instance: gpu-staging-04)

Context:
- Trying to load 'openvariant-xl-32k' from HF S3 mirror into our serving runtime for perf testing.
- Model is sharded into 8 files (pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.pt ...). Download pipeline uses our weights-fetcher service -> local cache -> runtime loader.
- Failure observed during checkpoint concat phase in loader (after all shards downloaded).

What I saw (timeline):
- 2024-10-03 09:12: kicked off rollout to dedicated pool on gpu-staging-04.
- 2024-10-03 09:17: first worker started downloads (logs below).
- 09:22: loader crashed with segmentation fault in C++ concat code. Process exit 139.
- Restarted, hit incomplete-shard error: loader complains missing file pytorch_model-00005-of-00008.pt even though fetcher reported success.
- After forcing re-download, got checksum mismatch on shard 00003, then OOM later on another run.

Commands tried and outputs (raw):
- curl to HF mirror (works, returns 200):
  curl -I https://hf-mirror.company.com/models/openvariant-xl-32k/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.pt
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK

- sha256sum check on downloaded shard (local cache):
  $ sha256sum /var/cache/weights/openvariant-xl-32k/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.pt
  1a2b3c...  /var/cache/weights/...  # expected 3f4e5d... -> mismatch
\- wget to re-download (succeeds but different checksum):
  $ wget https://hf-mirror.company.com/models/openvariant-xl-32k/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.pt -O /tmp/shard3.pt
  2024-10-03 09:28: downloaded 1.9G in 12s
  sha256sum /tmp/shard3.pt -> still 1a2b3c... (bad)

- gsutil copy from upstream bucket (succeeds, checksum matches expected):
  $ gsutil cp gs://hf-upstream/models/openvariant-xl-32k/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.pt /tmp/shard3_gs.pt
  sha256sum /tmp/shard3_gs.pt -> 3f4e5d... (expected)

Hypothesis 1: Our HF mirror or CDN corrupted shard 00003 during transfer. Evidence: direct upstream copy (gsutil) matches expected checksum; our mirror returns file but checksum different.
Hypothesis 2: Fetcher caching layer is renaming/overwriting files incorrectly under high concurrency -> missing/partial files (reports success but file truncated). Evidence: sometimes loader sees missing file even when fetcher logs "download complete".
Hypothesis 3: Checkpoint format mismatch: model was converted with new sharding tool v2 that uses slightly different header layout; our concat code mis-parses and segfaults when headers differ. Evidence: segfault location in concat C++ code around header parsing. However this doesn't explain checksum mismatch across sources.

Stack traces / log snippets (cleaned):
- worker log (09:22):
  [ERR] runtime/loader.cpp:412 concat_shards() Segmentation fault (signal 11) at 0x7f8b12c5
  #0  0x7f8b12c5 in memcpy \n  #1  0x55a3c8 in concat_shards
  (binary gulps core, no Python traceback)

- fetcher logs (09:15 - 09:30):
  INFO fetcher: starting download shard 00003 -> /var/cache/weights/openvariant-xl-32k/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.pt
  INFO fetcher: download complete, size=1903456890
  INFO fetcher: wrote metadata {etag: "abc123"} -> but no checksum field recorded (we rely on etag)

- loader error after restart (09:33):
  ERROR loader: missing shard file: /var/cache/weights/.../pytorch_model-00005-of-00008.pt

Reproduce steps tried locally (on dev laptop, m1/amd emulate):
- Re-run weights-fetcher with single-threaded downloads (concurrency=1) -> all shards downloaded, sha256 matches upstream (gsutil). Loader succeeded to concat.
- Run with concurrency=8 (default) -> sometimes one shard gets truncated (size smaller by a few bytes), loader complains.
- Use curl vs python requests vs boto S3 client -> different behavior depending on mirror (mirror returns truncated for some clients?), very odd.

Immediate next actions (TODOs):
- [ ] Add sha256 metadata verification to fetcher (compare against manifest) and fail early if mismatch. Right now we only record etag and size.
- [ ] Force fetcher to use ranged GET and verify content-length for each shard to detect truncation.
- [ ] Add temp file write + atomic rename after full download (avoid partial files being read). I think we already do atomic rename but need to re-check concurrency path.
- [ ] Run distributed test: simulate concurrency=8 against mirror, enable verbose HTTP logs (tcpdump?) to check for dropped connections.
- [ ] Open infra ticket for HF mirror (CDN) with example bad shard (attach both copies).
- [ ] Add more logging in concat_shards to validate header fields before memcpy to avoid segfault and emit meaningful errors.

Quick fixes / mitigation for rollout:
- Pin to upstream bucket (gs://hf-upstream) for now in staging config so fetcher uses canonical source (slower but verified).
- Add retry+verify layer: after download, compute sha256 and if mismatch then delete and retry up to 3 times.

Notes + random thoughts:
- Could be HTTP client bug where connection reuse returns wrong content-length header and truncated body is served from keep-alive buffer. Need to inspect HTTP client library and proxy.
- Check disk quotas on workers: truncated write could be caused by running out of disk mid-download -> but fetcher reported full size. Verify df -h and inode counts.
- For segfault: it's probably trying to memcpy based on header-provided size that doesn't match actual buffer -> add defensive bounds checks.

Files to attach to infra ticket:
- /var/cache/weights/openvariant-xl-32k/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.pt (bad copy)
- /tmp/shard3_gs.pt (good copy from gsutil)
- worker core dump (minidump) and loader binary version (git sha)
- fetcher logs (09:00-09:40)

Conversation notes from Slack: #eng-serve-runtime -> Jordan says mirror edge had incident on 2024-10-03 08:50-10:00, might be related. Maya suggested adding checksum to model manifests months ago (ticket MLF-199).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require manifest-level checksums for all uploads? (Pros: detect corruption early. Cons: requires regeneration of manifests + publishing process)
- Should fetcher prefer upstream storage when available despite cost? Probably default to mirror + verify, fallback to upstream on mismatch.

If I get blocked, escalate to SRE/infra with `JIRA-MLINF-412` and include both copies + reproduction steps.

End of scratchpad.
